pathogen.value: Marek's disease virus (MDV), an alphaherpesvirus in the genus Mardivirus

value: carried in dander shed from feather follicles
spread by breathing in contaminated dust/dander
the virus can survive for months in poultry house litter and dust

one leg stretched forward, one leg back is a typical stance in affected birds

mortality.value: in acute outbreaks, depression, paralysis and death can affect up to 80% of an unvaccinated flock
current, more virulent strains have caused mortality reaching 100% in unvaccinated chickens
outbreaks with mortality from tumors reaching 40-80% in chickens 8 to 17 weeks old have been reported in commercial flocks

incubation_period.value: microscopic changes appear about one to two weeks after infection, with visible (gross) lesions developing after three to four weeks
disease is seen from about 3-4 weeks of age onward, most often between 12 and 30 weeks of age

diagnosis.value: Diagnosis combines history and clinical signs, gross post-mortem findings (enlarged nerves and lymphoid tumors), and histological examination, with advanced lab methods such as immunohistochemistry, PCR and virus isolation used to confirm the diagnosis and rule out similar tumor diseases.

value: vaccination reduces the amount of virus shed even though it does not stop infection
keeping positive flocks closed with no birds added or removed
strict biosecurity and cleaning to cut down dander buildup
good diet and stress reduction to keep flocks healthier
vaccination
biosecurity

treatment_overview.value: There is no cure; supportive care such as a proper diet, parasite control and reducing stress can help affected flocks.
No treatment is available; infected birds do not recover.

summary.value: Marek's disease is a highly contagious herpesvirus infection of chickens that causes nerve damage, paralysis and tumors, spreading through dander shed from feather follicles. There is no cure once a bird is infected, but vaccination is highly effective at preventing the tumors and disease signs, even though vaccinated birds can still carry and spread the virus.
